text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Monday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Russia has promised never again to occupy the Baltic countries. Boris Yeltsin did not succeed to get a promise from Bill Clinton to exclude Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia from NATO expansion plans at the Helsinki summit.
- Lithuanians preferred to go to church on Palm Sunday than to election districts. The election commission said that 35.9 percent of people participated in the local elections on Sunday.

- Butinge Nafta oil terminal decided on Friday to boost its share capital to 260 million litas from 71.2 million litas. It is expected to sell the whole 188.7 million litas share issue to foreign investors.

- Lithuanian commercial banks have more free funds than reliable clients which need money. During the first two months of 1997, the interbank market was at a standstill with turnover at around 35 million litas.
- President Algirdas Brazauskas criticised the country's local election system. Brazauskas said it would be more democratic if people could vote both for the party lists and seperate candidates too.

- The total assets of all Lithuanian banks decreased in February by 3.7 million litas to 6.56 billion litas. Deposits also went down by 23.5 million litas to 4.97 billion litas, the Bank of Lithuania said.
- Communications Minister Rimantas Pleikys said that a bid to draw up a privatisation plan for Lithuanian Telecom will be announced at the end of March or in April.
- Rokishkis Cheese said it had 3.6 million litas profit during the two months of this year. The company is exempt from profit tax for three years since foreign investments exceed two million dollars.

- Germany's Siemens won the bid to computerise the information systems of Lithuanian Post. The suggested price was 8.5-10 times lower than that of the competitors. Some experts said Siemens was price dumping.
